settings.text: You already have a designer who draws flats in Illustrator, and you want a low-cost place to lay out tech packs and share them with your own factories.
You run many styles with factories you already trust, and you want grading rules, line sheets and production stages in one tool.
You want a software seat per person and you do not need anyone to make the product for you.
You do not have flats yet, or a tech designer or pattern maker. You want to pick a piece and get real flats and a checked pattern.
You want one partner from the idea to finished goods: samples, production and the factory, handled.
Your factory should get the pack in its own language (Chinese, Spanish, Portuguese or Italian), with every version kept.

settings.us: A design studio (the Design Lab) and a manufacturer. The Lab makes the pack; Future Basics samples and produces it.
settings.them: Tech pack and PLM software. Its site describes software only, with no sourcing or production service.

settings.us: Design Lab $499 for 90 days, or membership $100 a month. Your first tech pack is free, and the Make page gives a tech pack PDF of any piece you build there, no sign-up.
settings.them: Techpack Builder $35 per user per month, billed yearly ($420 a year). PLM Professional $95 and PLM Premium $125 per user per month, billed yearly. One-time onboarding: $100, $500 or $3,000.

settings.us: Build a piece on the Make page and download its tech pack, free, no sign-up.
settings.them: A 7-day free trial, no credit card. A 60-day money-back guarantee when bought with paid onboarding.

settings.us: Drawn for you from 382 professional flat sketches across 24 garment styles, front and back, measured in inches. Pick a base, add details, pick a colour.
settings.them: Its site lists image editing tools and an Adobe Illustrator plug-in. It does not say it draws flats for you.

settings.us: Points of measure come from the flats, graded XS to XXL, with tolerances.
settings.them: Measurement grading and automated grading rules (PLM Professional and up).

settings.us: Drafted from the measurements, and checked: every seam is walked to make sure the pieces sew together.
settings.them: Not mentioned on its pricing or home page.

settings.us: Future Basics makes it. Factories also get a link to the pack in their language, with messages on the pack.
settings.them: A team and factory collaboration hub and a manufacturer portal for the factories you already use.

settings.us: You can describe a piece in words to start it, or build it from the menu. Flats and patterns are drawn, not generated.
settings.them: Its site describes its PLM as an "AI-powered platform" but does not list specific AI features.

settings.heading: future basics or techpacker?
settings.lede: Both get you to a tech pack a factory can read. Techpacker is software for building and sharing tech packs: you bring the flats, the measurements and the factory. Future Basics draws them for you: the flats, the graded measurements and a pattern checked to sew together. Then we make the product.
